Clause-②: no — client-side link construction; no contract accept/reject change, no public surface widened.

**File surface — declared to REGION level, because this claim runs under a same-package parallelism exemption:**

- IN: the notification-centre / inbox feed region — `packages/app-shell/src/console/home/**`, `packages/app-shell/src/hooks/sharedInboxFeed*`, `packages/app-shell/src/chrome/notificationToast.tsx`, and their tests.
- ⛔ **OUT, hard**: `packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx`. That file is claimed by **#5176** in this same round (comment-5326259420, session `session_01AMHbqfPiETJHA95r6WzZWS`). `ConsoleShell.tsx` merely *imports* RecordDetailView for route wiring — reading it is fine, editing it is not. **If the fix turns out to require editing RecordDetailView.tsx, stop and report instead of editing it.**

**Serial constraints cleared:** `packages/app-shell` is co-occupied this round by #5176, which holds `views/RecordDetailView.tsx` only. Regions verified non-overlapping by inspection (`console/home/**` + `hooks/` + `chrome/` vs `views/RecordDetailView.tsx`). No open PR touches `packages/app-shell`.

**Maintainer authorisation for the parallel claim (2026-08-18):** the same-package serial rule is exempted for `packages/app-shell` at subdirectory-region granularity. The four replacement disciplines apply to this card and are not optional:
1. file surface declared to region level — done above;
2. merge `main` once before opening the PR;
3. merge `main` again after the sibling card (#5176) lands;
4. any conflict goes to the merge queue to arbitrate — ⛔ the PM does not hand-order, and you do not resolve a sibling's hunks.

## The card's own ruling (carry it; it is the acceptance floor)

> Pin it with a test asserting the **navigated URL**, not merely that navigation occurred — a test that only checks "the click went somewhere and mark-read fired" passes today.

That sentence is the whole card. A test that asserts navigation happened is worthless here, because that is exactly what passes against the bug.

## Why this is worth real care despite looking small

The two working controls are what make it severe, and they are already measured on the card: **mark-as-read fires correctly and is server-authoritative**, and **the canonical record route renders fine** (including in a `zh-CN` session). So the click consumes the notification, clears the badge, and drops the user on the app root — the pointer to the record is now *gone*, not merely inconvenient. Those two controls also narrow the fault to **link construction**, not routing and not rendering. Start there; do not go re-testing the route.

## Zone 2 — PM measurements (verify; I did not pin the exact component)

I located the region but not the defect. On `origin/main` @ `072085de` the notification surfaces are `chrome/notificationToast.tsx` (toasts), `console/ConsoleShell.tsx` (host wiring), and the inbox/home feed under `console/home/**` with `hooks/sharedInboxFeed*`; there is an existing test named `HomePage.inboxLinksTarget.test.tsx` that looks directly relevant — **read it first, it may already assert something adjacent to the bug.** Which of these actually builds the deep link is yours to establish.

## Fork clause

If the URL — or the record reference needed to build it — is **missing from the server's notification payload**, that half belongs to objectstack. Per the card: **file it back to `objectstack-ai/objectstack` with `Blocked-by:` linkage and do not widen this card.** Report `needs_decision` with the evidence rather than inventing a client-side reconstruction.

## Gates

Derive from your actual diff. Expect at minimum `Lint`, `Type Check`, the four `Test (shard N/4)` jobs, changeset gates, `Control Byte Scan`. That list is a clue, not a spec. Changeset required (`@object-ui/app-shell`, patch).

## Premise-first

The card is a QA-run finding with a named subject sha and two verified controls, so the premise is strong. If the link construction has since changed, follow what you measure — `premise_still_valid: false` with evidence is a legitimate delivery.

## Deliver

Draft PR against `main`, first line `Fixes #5179`. Push the branch early.

Return the structured JSON report AND post it as an issue comment whose first line is `<!-- os-dev-report -->`. Machine-checkable fields only.

**ACCEPT** — PR #5189 (`repo:objectui` seat PM, session `session_01AMHbqfPiETJHA95r6WzZWS`, reviewer of record).

**My file surface was wrong, in two separate ways, and the dev was right to go past it.** I wrote the IN surface as `console/home/**` + `hooks/sharedInboxFeed*` + `chrome/notificationToast.tsx`. Measured:
- `hooks/sharedInboxFeed*` **does not exist as a source file** — only test files match that glob; the real hook is `hooks/useHomeInbox.ts` over `hooks/sharedUserFeeds.ts`, and neither needed changing;
- `chrome/notificationToast.tsx` carries **no navigation or URL construction at all**, so it could never have been the defect site.

I said in the claim that I had located the region but not the defect. That was true, and two thirds of the region I named was noise. The dev found the actual site, declared the surface increment as the rule requires, and checked it against the four conditions rather than just widening. Correct behaviour — refusing to fix the notification centre because my guess pointed elsewhere would have been obedience at the cost of the card.

**The hard exclusion — the one that actually mattered — held.** `views/RecordDetailView.tsx` is not in the diff; I verified by `git diff --name-only`, not by report. All three parallel disciplines are satisfied and independently confirmed: the region was declared, and the branch contains **both** sibling merges (`6ca910bdf` for #5176 and `a09bc33ff` for #5141), so discipline 3 was met by construction rather than by promise.

**The diagnosis is the deliverable and it is complete — a chain, not a guess.** `action_url` is app-relative *by contract* (service-messaging `actionUrlFor()` synthesizes `/{object}/{id}` from the emit source, ADR-0030 L5, pinned upstream), so it names a record and the client must host it under an app. Home navigated it verbatim; the bell (`layout/InboxPopover.tsx`) hosted it under a raw `currentAppName ?? params.appName` and navigated it **bare** when neither named an app — which is the state on every surface mounting the bell outside `/apps/:appName/*` (`/home`, `/organizations`, full-page AI). A bare path matches no route, so the console catch-all forwards to `/`, and `RootLandingRedirect.resolveLandingPath()` returns the default app's root. That is the reported landing page, reached by a named mechanism at every step.

**The fork clause was correctly *not* invoked**: the server payload carries the deep link and is contract-correct, so nothing belongs back in objectstack. The card's scoping ("link construction, not routing or rendering") survived contact.

**The acceptance floor was met literally.** The card demanded assertions on the *navigated URL*, because a test that only checks navigation-occurred passes against the bug. Reverse verification reverted only the two component files and produced 6 red with a named failure — `expected '/showcase_task/t_42' to be '/apps/crm/showcase_task/t_42'` — while **6 controls stayed green in both states** (already-`/apps/` target, external link, no-link fallback, mark-read still fires). Keeping the collateral pins separate from the proving pins is what makes that evidence readable.

**One shared resolver, not two patched call sites.** `resolveNotificationTarget()` in `utils/appRoute.ts` reuses `resolveHostAppSegment` — the same resolution the two "see all" drills already used — and `HomePage.tsx`'s own comment already ruled that file the correct home so the two surfaces "cannot drift into two different answers for the same question". Fixing this as two independent patches would have rebuilt the very divergence that caused the bug.

**Platform note worth keeping:** the PR body needed a post-create repair because the GitHub sanitizer silently stripped raw `<Route …/>` / `<Navigate …/>` fragments *and* a `<default app>` placeholder (all `<`+letter), truncating two claims. It was rewritten without angle brackets **and read back to confirm** — the read-back is the part that turns a known hazard into a caught one.

**Out-of-scope finding #5190 verified present**, and it is the same defect *class* as this card rather than a stray: `mergeInboxRows` never maps `source_object`/`source_id` even though `InboxNotification` declares both and InboxPopover's back-compat arm reads them, so that arm is unreachable in the shipped tree — a notification without `action_url` marks itself read and navigates nowhere from the bell, while Home falls back to the full inbox. Same click, same data, two behaviours. Correctly left unfixed (retire-the-fields vs make-them-live is a product call) while still being routed through the new resolver so it can no longer build a bare path. That is the right treatment: neutralise the hazard, leave the decision.

**Landing:** path surface is `packages/app-shell/src/**` + changeset — no governed face, queue-eligible. CI not converged at review time (15 terminal: 13 success + 2 skipped; 6 running — four shards, Lint, Type Check). I flip ready and enqueue on terminal success of every required job, read by name.
